target_customer: Restaurants and hospitality groups, later finance teams across industries
problem: Restaurant operators process paper invoices by hand, which is slow and hides food cost data.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with payment services

technical_complexity.rationale: OCR to line item level with GL coding and accounting integrations was standard machine learning and integration work with some hard data capture parts.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with accounting and POS systems and accumulated invoice data raised switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition; the company stayed independent and rebranded as Ottimate in December 2023.

market_need_then: Restaurants recorded invoice data by hand into QuickBooks or Excel (YC blog, August 2015).

branding.domain_note: plateiq.com redirects to ottimate.com after the rebrand

identity.logo: Wordmark; Ottimate uses an octopus icon called Otti
identity.visual_style: Kept Plate IQ color palette in the rebrand
identity.voice_and_tone: Conversational voice for Ottimate to make AI approachable

branding.brand_signature: Don't just automate AP. Ottimate it.

rebrands.why: Name and visuals were restaurant only and limited expansion into other verticals (Altitude Marketing)

brand_strength.rationale: Plate IQ was a restaurant niche name that the company chose to outgrow; no evidence of brand driven growth.

pivots.to: AI AP automation for finance teams across industries

outcome_analysis: Plate IQ digitized restaurant invoices, raised a 4 million round in 2017 and a 160 million Series B led by FTV Capital in 2021, then rebranded to Ottimate in December 2023 to move beyond restaurants. It is active and growing, driven by a clear pain, integrations and later enterprise sales.
notes: Series B lead FTV Capital is from the YC company page and a Multiples.vc snippet; PYMNTS gives amount and label. A 500K seed in August 2015 appears only on Multiples.vc (aggregator), unverified. A third co-founder Shishir Deliwala appears only in one low quality profile, not listed. The 2017 round label is not stated by TechCrunch. Sourcery was named as a competitor only in 2017 coverage, outside the window, so no competitors recorded.
